newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends at 20-month high vs dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends at 20-month high vs dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at a 20-month high of 8.2924 on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2932 against the U.S. dollar on the Shanghai-based China foreign exchange interbank market.
Traders said the rise was mainly due to reduced intervention by the People's Bank of China, the central bank, which had sold the yuan heavily in early in the week to prevent it from rising sharply.
The rate toppled the former high of 8.2892 set on May 18, 1995. Trading was slow due the approach of the Chinese lunar new year holiday which begins on Thursday.

The yuan opened higher at 8.2926 and hit an intraday low of 8.2927 early in the session. It then rose steadily to move in a range of 8.2920 and 8.2924 for most of the session, hitting a high of 8.2900.
Most transactions were done at 8.2922, traders said.
One dealer said bidding on the yuan was heavy with the central bank reducing its intervention, but thin volume kept the currency's rising momentum to a minimum.
A second dealer said trading would be even slower on Thursday, the last trading day before the holiday.
"Tomorrow's transactions will be settled after the holiday according the exchange's T+1 settlement system," he said. "This will keep most traders from trading on Thursday."
Dealers expected the yuan to remain stable in the range of 8.2920 and 8.2930 on Thursday.
The yuan closed up at 6.7500 from 6.8000 against 100 Japanese yen and down at an intraday low of 1.0700 from 1.0688 against the Hong Kong dollar.
